title: Resident-set curator: slot-cohort KV residency + async eviction for GPU swap
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a resident-set curator that groups KV slots into small 'slot cohorts' and manages asynchronous eviction/prefetch pipelines to minimize synchronous GPU->host swaps under continuous batching. The goal is to reduce GPU paging events and allocator fragmentation while preserving latency SLOs for small and mid-sized conversational workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Resident-set curator prototype integrated with KV slab allocator and batch router deployed to perf cluster
Synthetic conversational workload shows >=25% reduction in GPU swap bytes/sec and >=15% reduction in swap-triggered p99 latency compared to baseline (runtime-1.18 behavior)
No regression in token-generation p50; p99 regression must be <=5% and justified with mitigation plan
End-to-end tests for crash/restart recovery ensure no KV corruption and deterministic refilling of cohorts
Observability: new metrics exposed (cohort_residency, async_eviction_inflight, staged_evicted_bytes) and dashboards added to Console runtime-2026.03
technical_notes: Slot cohorts: group contiguous KV slots by 'recency band' and estimated reuse window (0-50 tokens, 50-200 tokens, >200 tokens). Cohort is an append-only ring of slot descriptors with per-cohort residency budget in bytes.

Resident-set curator responsibilities: track cohort budgets, schedule async write-back of cold slots to host staging (pinned host pool), coordinate micro-compaction to reduce fragmentation, and instruct batch router about affinity tokens.

Async eviction pipeline: batched coalesced cudaMemcpyAsync from GPU pages to pinned host buffers -> NVMe staging if needed. Eviction is non-blocking for request-path; requests hitting a slot marked 'evicting' see a soft miss path with prioritized prefetch.
Prefetch and hints: continuous-batching heuristics emit prefetch hints based on the most recent sequence-length histogram for a request source; prefetches are ranked and scheduled per-cohort.

Allocator integration: add cohort-aware free lists and a lightweight micro-compaction step that merges adjacent free segments within a cohort when free fraction > 30% to avoid long tail fragmentation.

Concurrency model: curator uses a lock-free ring for cohort descriptors and a single writer per-GPU stream for eviction commands to avoid cross-stream synchronization. GPU stream-affinity tokens are attached to batched requests to sequence KV reads and avoid implicit synchronizations.

Fallback policy: if async eviction queue backs up, curator triggers 'hard-evict' policy that pauses low-priority batch traffic (dedicated/guest flag) and escalates to multi-batch coalesced DMA to free space quickly.

Metrics & instrumentation: cohort_count, cohort_resident_bytes, cohort_budget_pct, async_eviction_inflight, avg_eviction_batch_size, swap_failures, micro_compact_count, allocator_frag_pct. Export via runtime telemetry and show per-model breakdown.

Security considerations: evicted data flushed to ephemeral encrypted staging (KMS-protected) and cleared on deallocation. Ensure no plaintext KV remains in pinned host pool longer than retention threshold (configurable).
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Spike completed. Validated that grouping by recency band reduces conflict evictions in microbenchmarks. Prototype design doc created in Confluence.
2026-02-25: Implemented cohort descriptors and residency bookkeeping in allocator branch. Basic async eviction pipeline using pinned host buffers works end-to-end in unit tests.

2026-03-03: Bench results on perf-cluster-2: swap_bytes/sec reduced from ~12% to ~4% for 'multi-turn-chat-small' workload. Observed a p99 latency bump for tail cases when cohort budget under-provisioned.
2026-03-06: Added backpressure signals to batch router to avoid overcommitting cohorts; mitigated p99 regression to within 3%.

2026-03-09: Code review feedback requested changes to eviction retry/backoff and KMS staging lifecycle. Addressing comments in PR #5243. Running extended soak test to validate micro-compaction stability.
2026-03-10: Soak test shows stable memory fragmentation under sustained mixed workloads. Preparing dashboard tiles and release notes for runtime-2026.03 canary rollout.
decisions: Use fixed recency bands (0-50, 51-200, 201+) for initial cohort definitions; will evaluate adaptive bands in follow-up if needed.
Eviction is write-back (to encrypted host staging) and non-blocking by default; synchronous hard-eviction reserved for emergency/backpressure.
Prefetch hints sourced from continuous-batching router rather than model-level heuristics to reduce cross-team surface area and leverage existing histograms.
Micro-compaction is best-effort and runs in a low-priority background thread to avoid upsetting SLOs.
risks: Underprovisioned cohort budgets can cause repeated prefetches and increased latency for tail requests; mitigation: auto-tune budgets and expose knobs in Console.
Pinned host buffer exhaustion under large-scale eviction bursts; mitigation: global staged_bytes limit with backpressure to batch router.
Complex interactions between batch affinity tokens and third-party model code that uses explicit CUDA streams; plan to add opt-out and safe-fallback path.
KMS/staging lifecycle introduces extra dependencies and potential latency when writing evicted pages; evaluate per-customer configuration to disable NVMe staging for latency-sensitive tenants.
